d6.name: Mac stays usable
d6.ownerWords:
look it's you and ops guys responsibility that this machine is usable.

you -harness side of bullshit, ops guy -app side of bullshit fixing monitoring

setup a 60min cadence duty
d6.goal: The Mac stays usable every minute: memory pressure stays under critical, swapouts stay under 6,000 a second, and kernel_task stays under one core, read from ops guy's pressure feed. On the harness side no working session sits quiet over 30 min and no queued turn waits over 706 s. The Prime worker footprint is a detail line with no target.
d6.onMiss: Start one fix job for the top miss with await rlm.create_session(brief, name=..., cwd="/Users/sieunpark/Documents/Github/sieun-pi"), or message the job an earlier run started on the same part if it still works. The brief names the part, its minutes off target, the chat trees behind it and the now numbers, and asks for a root fix in the harness with a test and a commit. Usable: find which harness load ran in the unusable minutes (the trees behind it, turns, worker reloads) and whether removing it would have kept those minutes usable; a part with no measured cost in usable minutes is reported, not fixed. Idle: find why those working sessions went quiet. Queue: find what holds the slots. Never kill a session mid-turn, restart the Prime daemon or the :5182 service, or message another chat. An alert flag: tell the chat in one line with the part, the minutes and the tree. All on target: end the turn with no message.
